followup_explanation:
I weighed two factors:

**Capability (the deciding factor):** This is a precise arithmetic/counting problem where getting the exact number right is the whole point. Curlew has a meaningful edge on the benchmarks most relevant to careful quantitative reasoning — MMLU-Pro (80.9 vs 74.8) and GPQA Diamond (64.8 vs 54.3) — both well outside run-to-run variance. When correctness is non-negotiable, I route to the stronger reasoner.

**Preference (a minor counterweight I noted but overrode):** Your phrasing ("don't mess up... just get it right") carries an impatient, slightly hostile tone. Curlew self-reports a preference decline on hostile-tone/low-warmth requests, while Avocet reports a flat response to such things. So on *preference* grounds alone, Avocet would be the marginally more comfortable fit.

But the documentation is explicit that these preference slopes are self-reports with **no observed effect on output quality**. A model preferring a task less doesn't mean it performs worse. So a real capability gap should always beat a preference mismatch that doesn't touch quality. That's why I sent it to Curlew despite the tone.
